nodes.summary: Every finite set $M$ of natural numbers contains a homothetic copy of the empty set.
nodes.title: Every finite set contains a copy of the empty set

nodes.summary: Let $S$ and $M$ be finite sets of natural numbers. $M$ contains a homothetic copy of $S$ if there are a natural number $a > 0$ and an integer $b$ such that $as + b \in M$ for every $s \in S$, that is, $aS + b \subseteq M$. This is Maker's winning condition.
nodes.title: Containing a homothetic copy

nodes.summary: For every finite set $A$ of rational numbers, $A$ is a copy of $A$.
nodes.title: Every finite set of rationals is a copy of itself

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of rational numbers. $B$ is a copy of $A$ if there are rationals $a > 0$ and $b$ such that $B = aA + b = \{ax + b : x \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Copies of finite sets of rationals

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets of rational numbers. $B$ is a reflection of $A$ if there are rationals $a < 0$ and $b$ such that $B = aA + b = \{ax + b : x \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Reflections of finite sets of rationals

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers with at least two elements. If Maker, moving first with no numbers claimed, can force a win in the game on $S$ within $|S|$ selections, then $S$, viewed as a set of rational numbers, is symmetric.
nodes.title: A fast Maker win forces symmetry

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of rational numbers with $n \ge 4$ elements. If $S$ is symmetric of type $(i, j)$, with positions counted from $0$, then $(i, j)$ is $(0, n - 1)$, $(1, n - 1)$ or $(0, n - 2)$. In the paper's one-based numbering these are the types $(1, n)$, $(2, n)$ and $(1, n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Possible types of a symmetric set

nodes.summary: A finite set $S$ of rational numbers with at least four elements is symmetric of at most one type: if $S$ is symmetric of types $(i, j)$ and $(i', j')$, then $i = i'$ and $j = j'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the symmetry type

nodes.summary: Let $S = \{s_0 < s_1 < \dots < s_{n-1}\}$ be a finite set of $n$ rational numbers and let $i, j < n$. Then $S$ is called symmetric of type $(i, j)$ if $i < j$ and $S \setminus \{s_i\}$ is a copy of $S \setminus \{s_j\}$.
nodes.title: Symmetric sets of a given type

nodes.summary: A finite set $S$ of rational numbers is symmetric if it is symmetric of some type $(i, j)$ with $i, j < |S|$.
nodes.title: Symmetric sets of rationals

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a finite set of natural numbers with $|S| \le 3$, then, starting from the position where no number has been claimed, Maker wins the $S$-game within $|S|$ moves.
nodes.title: Maker wins the $S$-game in $|S|$ moves when $|S| \le 3$

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a set of four natural numbers, then, starting from the position where no number has been claimed, Maker wins the $S$-game within $5$ moves.
nodes.title: Maker wins the $S$-game in five moves when $|S| = 4$

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a set of four natural numbers, then, starting from the position where no number has been claimed, Maker wins the $S$-game within $4$ moves if and only if $S$, viewed as a set of rationals, is symmetric.
nodes.title: Four-element sets with a four-move win are the symmetric ones

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers with $|S| = n$, and let $N$ be a natural number such that every 2-coloring of $S^N$ has a monochromatic combinatorial line. Then, starting from the position where no number has been claimed, Maker wins the $S$-game within $\lceil n^N / 2 \rceil$ moves.
nodes.title: Hales–Jewett bound for the $S$-game

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $p$ a natural number. Let $T$ be a finite rooted tree with root $r$ whose vertices are pairwise distinct rationals, such that every path from $r$ down to a vertex has at most $p$ vertices and some such path has exactly $p$ vertices (so $T$ has height $p - 1$). Suppose that for every leaf $v$ the set of vertices on the path from $r$ to $v$ contains a copy $aS + b$ of…
nodes.title: Tree criterion for fast wins

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers, and let $M$ and $B$ be finite sets of natural numbers. Maker wins the $S$-game within $0$ moves from the position where Maker has claimed $M$ and Breaker has claimed $B$ if and only if $M$ contains a copy $aS + b = \{as + b : s \in S\}$ of $S$, where $a$ is a positive integer and $b$ is an integer.
nodes.title: Winning within zero moves

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers. In the $S$-game, Maker and Breaker alternately claim unclaimed natural numbers, and Maker wins once the numbers Maker has claimed contain a copy $aS + b = \{as + b : s \in S\}$ of $S$, where $a$ is a positive integer and $b$ is an integer. Let $M$ and $B$ be finite sets of natural numbers (claimed by Maker and by Breaker) and $p$ a natural number, with Maker to move.…
nodes.title: Maker wins within $p$ moves

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a finite set of natural numbers with $|S| \ge 5$, then, starting from the position where no number has been claimed, Maker does not win the $S$-game within $|S|$ moves.
nodes.title: Maker cannot win the $S$-game in $|S|$ moves when $|S| \ge 5$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every rational $k$, $S_2(n + 2, k) = \{0\} \cup \{k^i : 0 \le i \le n\} = \{0, 1, k, \dots, k^n\}$.
nodes.title: The zero-geometric set $S_2(n + 2, k)$

nodes.summary: Let $S = \{s_0 < s_1 < \dots < s_{n-1}\}$ be a finite set of $n$ rational numbers, and let $i, j < n$ be such that $S$ is symmetric of type $(i, j)$, with positions counted from $0$. If $i = 1$ and $j = n - 1$, then there is a rational number $k > 1$ such that the zero-geometric set $S_2(n, k)$ is a copy of $S$. If $i = 0$ and $j = n - 2$, then there is a rational number $k > 1$ such that $S_2(n, k)$ is a…
nodes.title: Zero-geometric copies of symmetric sets

nodes.summary: For every rational number $k$, the zero-geometric set $S_2(1, k)$ equals $\{0\}$.
nodes.title: The zero-geometric set $S_2(1, k)$ is $\{0\}$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a rational number $k$, $S_2(n, k)$ is the finite set of rationals $\{0\} \cup \{k^i : 0 \le i < n - 1\}$, that is, $\{0, 1, k, \dots, k^{n-2}\}$ when $n \ge 2$ and $\{0\}$ when $n \le 1$.
nodes.title: The zero-geometric set $S_2(n, k)$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
